digest.component_or_area: reconciler git mutation policy gate (check_raw_git_writes.py, R3 composition rule)
propositions: The existing gate (policy d37e) enforces mechanism-level rules R1/R2 (no raw subprocess git) but misses protocol violations: callers composing sanctioned git-adapter primitives (e.g., git_adapter.add + git_adapter.commit in reconcile_helpers.py:226/246) execute outside the atomic transaction without triggering any violation.

R3 composition rule extends the gate to fire on calls to git-adapter mutation primitives (add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree) made from outside the reconciler write-seam modules (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py, _pass_lock_lifecycle.py), by resolving git-adapter receiver bindings (import and dynamic-loader forms) per file.
R3 does not fire on read-only exports (commit_email, rev_parse), non-git-adapter .add()/.commit() calls (set, session), or mutations inside the sanctioned seam files themselves.

Both remaining out-of-transaction sites (reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 and __main__.py:338-351, now _pass_lock_lifecycle.py:338-351) receive durable reasoned inline # raw-git-ok: markers rather than debt baselines; markers are reused from the existing vocabulary and failure is still enforced on reason-less markers (marker-without-reason violation).

The seam split (extracting _pass_lock_lifecycle.py containing _purge_committed_reconciler_locks and related lock-lifecycle functions) reduces __main__.py below the module-size gate threshold and serves as an end-to-end check that R3 applies correctly outside the exemption set.

R3's first run on the real tree (origin/main 0b851c8103) enumerated exactly 7 hits across 2 functions with zero false positives in src/ + scripts/, confirming the receiver-binding strategy does not fire on ordinary .add()/.commit() calls.
